issues.description: Constructor/class name mismatch in the example bitmap header: the template's example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares the class as Image24 but declares constructors named Bitmap24(), which does not match the class name. The solution repository uses class name Bitmap24. This mismatch in the template will cause compilation failures and confuses students about the correct API to implement/use (Bitmap24 vs Image24). The problem statement requires the assignment to compile, so this structural inconsistency prevents students from building the provided example and following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header to Bitmap24 (replace 'class Image24' with 'class Bitmap24') so that the class name matches the declared constructors and the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp. Alternatively, if 'Image24' is intended, rename the constructors and implementation to Image24 consistently across example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp and related files. Ensure the template matches the solution's API (Bitmap24) so students can compile and use the example program as intended.

issues.description: The header in the template declares the class as Image24 (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) while the implementation and usage refer to Bitmap24 (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp). The solution header defines class Bitmap24. This mismatch between the header class name and the implemented/expected name (and the header file name) will confuse students: the header file is named Bitmap24.hpp but exposes Image24, breaking the clear mapping from file -> class -> implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header from Image24 to Bitmap24 to match the file name and the implementation (or alternatively rename implementation and all references to Image24). Specifically, update example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp: change 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' and ensure constructors/destructor signatures remain consistent.
